evidence: Hays — project Master Plant Pool contains 44 wild observations and a Hays-local flag for Senna lindheimeriana.
Travis — UT Plant Resources Center provides a dedicated Travis County treatment.
Val Verde — Amistad vascular-plant inventory documents the species as common on rocky flats, slopes, outcrops, and ledges.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Hays count uses the project's wild-observation pool; the Purola introduced planting is not used as native-range evidence.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with the foliage texture and stature. Lindheimer's senna is a tall perennial with several velvety stems, 4–8 pairs of oblong leaflets, and conspicuously soft-hairy gray-green foliage. Yellow flowers cluster in upper leaf axils.
diagnostic_traits: erect bushy habit, often over 1 m
yellow 5-petaled flowers in upper axillary clusters

confusers.separator: S. roemeriana has only one pair of leaflets per leaf; S. lindheimeriana has 4–8 pairs and a much more velvety gray-green look.
S. pilosior is an annual Trans-Pecos/desert species; S. lindheimeriana is a perennial Edwards Plateau/Trans-Pecos species with a woody root and taller velvety habit.
